reviews.title: This monitor didn’t just change my setup I now see in 4K, and possibly in the fourth dimension
reviews.comment: Let me preface this by saying I’ve never written a review longer than a haiku, but the ASUS 27” 4K Eye Care Monitor (VY27UQ) deserves a literal standing ovation—and since I sit for 14 hours a day, that’s saying something. I bought this because my previous monitor was about as vibrant as a DMV waiting room. When I upgraded to this majestic beast of pixels, it was like removing a film from my eyeballs that had been there since 2002. I loaded up a 4K wallpaper of a mountain range and I’m pretty sure a hawk flew out of the screen and nested on my ceiling. That’s how real it looks. Let’s break this beauty down: UHD 3840 x 2160: This isn’t just Ultra High Definition. This is Ultra Holy-Cow-I-Can-Count-The-Pores-On-This-YouTuber’s-Nose Definition. IPS Panel: The colors are so consistent from every angle that I now invite guests over just to sit beside me and whisper, “Look at the reds, Brad. Just LOOK at them.” HDR10: I watched a documentary about mushrooms and the spores basically levitated out of the screen. It’s like being part of a planetarium exhibit that cost $249 and came with free shipping. Adaptive Sync: My games no longer tear like emotionally unstable relationships. I play, it adapts. I cry a little. Not out of lag, but out of joy. Eye Care Plus / Blue Light Filter / Flicker Free: My eyes used to dry out faster than hotel shampoo. Now? They’re practically spa-treated. I stare at this monitor for hours and my retinas send me thank-you notes. Built-in speakers: Are they audiophile grade? No. But will they save your butt during a Zoom call when your headphones are tangled in a knot made by a spiteful ghost? Absolutely. DisplayWidget: I didn’t even know I needed this until I started using it. Now I adjust brightness and color like I’m piloting the bridge of the Starship Enterprise. 3-Year Warranty: I’ve had shorter romantic relationships than this warranty. ASUS believes in this monitor more than I believe in finishing my laundry. Let’s be real: For $249, this is probably the best thing I’ve ever bought that didn’t require monthly payments, a therapist’s approval, or a permission slip from my significant other. I now gaze lovingly at this screen even when it's off. My productivity is up, my gaming has improved, and I’m pretty sure I look slightly cooler just sitting next to it. My cat has started sleeping in front of it like it’s a tiny sun. Final thoughts: If you need a monitor, this is it. If you don’t need a monitor, you’re wrong. Buy it. Mount it. Bask in it. And when someone comes over and says, “Wow, that’s a nice monitor,” you can lean back, nod slowly, and whisper: “It’s more than a monitor. It’s a lifestyle.”
reviews.author: Ken K

reviews.title: A Monitor That Delivers
reviews.comment: Here’s what stands out: • The 4K resolution is actually crisp. Not “looks great if you squint.” This thing is razor-sharp whether you’re deep in spreadsheets or pretending to write your next bestseller. • IPS panel with HDR10 = real color accuracy. If you’re doing design work (or just want your emails to look majestic), it holds up. • Adaptive Sync keeps everything smooth. No screen tearing, no weird stutters—just clean visuals, whether it’s meetings, edits, or YouTube “research.” Bonus: The stand doesn’t wobble like a cheap lawn chair, and it doesn’t look like it was designed by a discount gaming brand trying too hard. Bottom line: If you want a monitor that works like it’s supposed to, looks how it’s supposed to, and won’t make your eyes beg for mercy after a 10-hour day—this is the one.
reviews.author: Greg Moody

reviews.title: Hot trash
reviews.comment: Complete trash. Had installed less than one month with minimal use, started making noise then turned itself diff. Too late to return and shipping back to manufacturer is half the price of  what I paid. Don’t waste your cash.
reviews.author: Jordan A. Jackson

reviews.title: Wonderful Value
reviews.comment: For the money, this monitor is a great deal. The picture in SDR is bright and clear with great contrast. HDR looks kinda "meh", but at this price point you shouldn't expect anything fancy. The built-in speakers sound very "tinny" and should be fine if you're listening to podcasts, but for music, movies, and gaming, you will want proper speakers. One minor con: I noticed this monitor has a distinct humming sound when in a totally quiet space; this could be annoying to some. However with enough background noise, you wouldn't notice it.
